findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently discards the original 4-arg method
findings.body: The pre-existing method `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (lines 145-147) is immediately redefined by a new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151). In Ruby, the second definition silently replaces the first in the method table (producing a 'method redefined' warning), so any existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, max_width, max_height, opts)` with separate width/height arguments (e.g. thumbnail-creation code elsewhere in the app that previously relied on this 4-positional-argument signature) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments` at runtime, because the surviving method only accepts 3 positional arguments plus an options hash. This breaks any existing thumbnail/downsize call site that isn't in this diff, not just the new feature path.

findings.title: Animated GIF detection never triggers because tempfile paths have no extension
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` passes `tempfile.path` as the `from` argument. Inside `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the check `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb line 155) decides whether to use the gifsicle-based animated instructions. Rack/ActionDispatch tempfiles typically have no file extension (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart...`), so this regex will never match for uploads coming through this new code path. As a result, large animated GIFs that need downsizing will always go through the regular ImageMagick `downsize_instructions`, which selects only the first frame (`#{from}[0]`), silently stripping the animation from any animated GIF that exceeds `max_image_size_kb`.

findings.title: Downsizing loop ignores failure and may silently upload an oversized image
findings.body: The loop at lines 64-70 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value. `convert_with` (and therefore `downsize`) returns `false` on any ImageMagick/gifsicle failure (e.g. missing binary, malformed input, unsupported geometry string). If downsizing fails on every attempt, the loop exits solely because `attempt` reaches 0, and the code proceeds to call `Upload.create_for` with the original oversized `tempfile` and no error is surfaced to the caller or the user. This defeats the purpose of the size check and can let files larger than the configured `max_image_size_kb` through unnoticed.

findings.title: API URL download size limit hardcoded to 10MB regardless of site settings
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` limit with a fixed 10MB constant. Since `type` can represent non-image attachments as well as images, this removes any admin-configurable control over how large a file the server will fetch via the API URL path (e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb`), silently allowing downloads up to 10MB even on sites configured with a much smaller limit, and wasting bandwidth/memory for attachments that cannot later be downsized.

findings.title: Client-side max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring configured site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, honoring separate admin-configured limits for images (`max_image_size_kb`) and attachments (`max_attachment_size_kb`). It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB for both types. Attachments cannot be downsized server-side the way images can, so an admin who configured a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will no longer have that limit enforced client-side; uploads up to 10MB will be attempted and only fail (if at all) after the fact, producing a confusing UX and bypassing the admin's intended restriction. The same hardcoding is repeated for the 413 (entity too large) error message at line 246, which previously reported `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and can now show an incorrect max size to users if the server's actual limit differs from 10MB.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic downsizing feature
findings.body: The PR adds a new downsize-on-upload code path (lines 63-70) plus corresponding API changes in `optimized_image.rb` (collapsing `downsize` to a 3-arg/percent-based signature), but no tests were added or updated to cover: downsizing being triggered when `max_image_size_kb` is exceeded, the loop giving up after 5 attempts, or the behavior change to `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s signature. Given this changes both a public model API and upload behavior, the lack of tests makes it easy for the regressions noted above (duplicate method definition, lost GIF animation, silent oversized uploads) to go unnoticed before release.
